weapon.story.wp002521.4: She might be imagining the similarities, yet she can't throw the\ngun away—so she stuffs it into the bag on the back of her motorbike\nand rides off.
weapon.story.wp002522.1: Ten years ago: His home was unsafe, his parents murdered in\nexchange for coins. As he no longer needed his spear to fish, he\ntook weapon in hand and set out in search of the killer.
weapon.story.wp002522.2: Five days ago: The city was in a state of neglect, as usual. Every day, someone else died—a stranger, a neighbor, a friend. Why does it always have to be this way? he lamented to himself.
weapon.story.wp002522.3: Yesterday: He found the man who killed his parents and plunged\nhis spear into the criminal's heart. Finally, after ten long years, his\nfamily had been avenged.
weapon.story.wp002522.4: Now: <i>What if that was the wrong man? What if someone else\nwas the true killer?<i> With spear in hand, the man grins wildly\nand sets off in search of the killer.
weapon.story.wp002523.1: From where are we born? To where do we go?\nThere is no way to know, for a life enters this world with no\nrecollection of what transpired even a moment before.
weapon.story.wp002523.2: A life brought into this world vanishes without taking form, ever\nunaware of who they are or what feelings they have gained.
weapon.story.wp002523.3: A freed life inherits the feelings of her older sister. But once\nshe fulfills this wish, where will she go next?
weapon.story.wp002523.4: From where are we born? To where do we go?\nThere is no need to ask such questions, because it is impossible\nto know what tomorrow holds.
weapon.story.wp002524.1: I've recently come to think of myself as a terrible man who\nneglected his family for years in order to pursue his own selfish\nadventures.
weapon.story.wp002524.2: I never used to know homesickness. But these days, images of my\nfamily surface in my mind whenever I travel. And now that I miss\nthem, my skills are starting to slip.
weapon.story.wp002524.3: I've caused my wife and my daughter nothing but trouble. I know\nthis—I've known it the entire time. But my inarticulate nature and\nstubborn pride always got in the way of change.
weapon.story.wp002524.4: Next time I go home, I'll muster up my courage and tell them what\nI feel. I'll tell them I'm sorry for causing so much pain over the\nyears. Yes, the next time I go home, I will...
weapon.story.wp003002.1: One day, a man's daughter was captured by enemy soldiers.\nDesperate, he purchased a weapon with a shady history and\nset off to save his child.
weapon.story.wp003002.2: Suddenly, the shady weapon said to him,\n"Me and myself will help you." The young voice reminded him\nof his daughter, and the flames of his anger rose higher.
weapon.story.wp003002.3: Though battered and bruised, he managed to save his daughter.\nAs tears rolled down his cheeks, he told the weapon,\n"You saved my family. Thank you."
weapon.story.wp003002.4: "Family"? Never heard of it. I don't need anyone besides me,\nmyself, and you. No one, got it?\nAll this world needs is me, myself, and you."
weapon.story.wp003003.1: Once, in a kingdom far away, there were three laws imposed on the\npeople by the royal family. Violating a law would result in harsh\npunishments or even death, but most citizens still praised them.
weapon.story.wp003003.2: The first law was "Do not steal." This obviously included theft\nand burglary, but also life—and once there was even a dispute as\nto whether "stealing one's heart" counted.
weapon.story.wp003003.3: The second law was "Do not harm another's reputation." Though it\nseemed a kindly law, it was actually enacted to avoid damaging the\ndignity of the kingdom through language or insult.
weapon.story.wp003003.4: The third law was a secret, which the people loved, for they felt it\nmade everyone more considerate. Alas, no one realized it was done\nsimply so the royal family could execute whomever they wished.
weapon.story.wp003005.1:
There once lived a small, shabby bird in a far-off forest.
This bird was often ridiculed by its fellows for its dull and scruffy
wings, but the bird paid no mind as these wings allowed it to
soar through the great sky it loved so dearly.
weapon.story.wp003005.2:
Unhappy seeing such filthy wings in their sky, the other birds
made a proposal. "Let us see who can fly the highest. Win and
our wings will be yours; lose and you must leave this forest."
Wishing for beautiful wings, the bird accepted.
weapon.story.wp003005.3:
The match begins and all the birds take to the sky.
As they climb, the air thins and the currents grow unpredictable,
and before long only the small bird and a sea eagle remain.
The small bird reaches its limit, and is unable to go on.
weapon.story.wp003005.4:
The small bird crashes toward the ground. Just before it meets
land, it is lit up by the sun and engulfed in flames. The beauty
with which it soared through the air as fire ravaged its body was
said to rival that of the legendary phoenix.
weapon.story.wp003006.1: TYPE-4O BLADE INSTRUCTION MANUAL: Before use, confirm all\nattachments are accounted for. Use the tester on initial\nstart-up to check for energization.
weapon.story.wp003006.2: WARNING! Refrain from using this product if you suffer from\ndefects in mobility or calculative capacity. Do not wield it\nfor cases outside its intended use.
weapon.story.wp003006.3: CARE INSTRUCTIONS: After battle, use a soft cloth and light\ncleaning liquid to remove any dirt. In case of physical damage to\nthe product, please consult your Operator.
weapon.story.wp003006.4: DISCLAIMER: This product does not conform to military product\nsafety standards. YoRHa R&D is not liable for injury or death\nsuffered due to use of this product regardless of cause.
weapon.story.wp003007.1: I am the emperor of this great nation. My governance is absolute,\nmy word law—though I doubt any would dare speak their mind\nbefore a blade so great as this. Do you not agree?
weapon.story.wp003007.2:
This wonderful blade can sever a dozen heads in one blow,
so neighboring countries dare not touch my lands. Ah, but this
makes life dull; I must let my blade indulge in blood sometimes,
you see.
weapon.story.wp003007.3:
Let us eradicate the nation to the south! I hear there are many
lovely women there, so take whichever you like. Meanwhile, I will
cut through the advance guard and see how many heads I can
claim.
weapon.story.wp003007.4:
A dozen enemies surround me, so with one fell sweep,
I will... wait. What are you doing? Why have you turned your
blade on me!? You make thirteen, which means my blade...
will...not...
weapon.story.wp003009.1: I remember skin, pale and soft.\nNot taut and cold like this.
weapon.story.wp003009.2: I remember a voice, clear and melodic.\nNot low and gravelly like this.
weapon.story.wp003009.3: I remember hair, long and glossy.\nNot short and wiry like this.
weapon.story.wp003009.4: I remember eyes, lonely and sad.\nNot ones that crave me like this.
weapon.story.wp003010.1: Humans are extremely selfish creatures that oppose any who are\ndifferent. Thus do they make displays of their power,\nwith winners holding sway over losers.
weapon.story.wp003010.2: Humans revere the continuation of their own species—they are\nattracted to one another and breed. Thus do more come into being,\ngiving rise to new victims.
weapon.story.wp003010.3: Humans are unable to exist alone—they constantly seek\nconnections with others. Thus do their gatherings become\ndisorderly mobs without purpose.
weapon.story.wp003010.4: Humans are foolish and unsalvageable creatures. Is there any need\nto allow them to live?\nNo. All humans deserve to die diE dIe DIe DiE DIE DIE
weapon.story.wp003011.1: We were wed as the minister arranged. We did so for our family,\nand for future generations. I had no interest in love or romance,\nand had no reservations toward this marriage.
weapon.story.wp003011.2: I remember how unwelcoming she looked when I first laid eyes on\nher. This aura made her hard to approach; I hesitated to even\nspeak with her. How does she view this marriage? I often wondered.
weapon.story.wp003011.3:
She surrendered her young life for the sake of her house,
so I understood if she shut off her heart. I pitied her, and tried
to be considerate and understanding. We were husband and wife,
after all.
weapon.story.wp003011.4: But she remained detached; more like a doll than a living being.\nThinking of her that way, my efforts started to feel foolish. What\nhad I been hoping for? I should have just done this from the start.
weapon.story.wp003012.1:
There was once a world filled with light which ate
away at life and withered the land. But one rebelled
against fate and fought the light with his black 
greatsword—one known as the Warrior of Darkness.
weapon.story.wp003012.2:
Warped by light, the sin eaters dragged the world
toward destruction. But as the warrior continued his
journey, the light began to eat away at him, and he
lost the strength to wield his greatsword.
weapon.story.wp003012.3:
When his last foe fell, light spilled from the warrior,
transforming the hero into one who pushed back the
dark. Yet even so, his sword supported him, and he
found the strength to continue on.
weapon.story.wp003012.4:
He defeated the ancient mage. He snuffed out the
primordial hero. The Warrior of Darkness persevered
through adversity and returned darkness to the sky,
thus the people named his sword "Shadowbringer."
weapon.story.wp003013.1:
The army gave me a standard-issue sword—a tiny, flimsy thing. 
I need to find a better weapon so I can kill more enemies 
and earn more money. Otherwise, 
what's the point of risking my life?
weapon.story.wp003013.2:
One day, I see a guy in my squad 
mowing down hundreds of foes with 
a sword as tall as himself. At that moment, 
I know it is the weapon for me.
weapon.story.wp003013.3:
Eventually I end up fighting beside 
the man and his huge sword. As he battles, 
I plunge my useless sword into his back. And after 
watching him die, I take up his greatsword for myself.
weapon.story.wp003013.4:
But I can't stand to see such a beautiful blade soaked with blood, 
so I sell it off and gained more money than 
I could spend in a lifetime. 
Then I quit the army to live out my days in peace.
weapon.story.wp003015.1:
Once, the citizens of a small and
quiet nation crafted an elegant white bell in
the hopes that their days of peace might last forever.
Placed in the palace, it would be rang every day when
it was time for prayer.
weapon.story.wp003015.2:
Made of a very special metal,
it made a sound unlike any other bell.
When the citizens heard it,
they would turn in the direction of the palace and pray,
thankful for the peace they enjoy.
weapon.story.wp003015.3:
But no peace lasts forever, and war came before long.
With little military to speak of,
the country was devastated in an instant.
Its palace was left in ruins,
and the white bell was nowhere to be found.
weapon.story.wp003015.4:
The bell was melted down and made into swords to
be wielded by soldiers—the country's former citizens.
The swords are every bit as beautiful as the bell was,
but the sound they make on
the battlefield is a thing of horrors.
weapon.story.wp003017.1:
There once was a nobleman who collected all manner of 
curios—weapons, armor, art, and whatever else caught 
his eye. One day, a peddler came to him and 
said he had a fine item in stock.
weapon.story.wp003017.2:
The peddler had a mechanical doll that did all manner of tasks. 
At first, the nobleman refused, but he finally 
decided to rent her for a spell, and soon found 
himself enjoying her company.
weapon.story.wp003017.3:
Eventually, the peddler came to reclaim the rented doll. 
But the lonely noble could not imagine parting with her,
so he paid the peddler a great deal of 
money to keep her around.
weapon.story.wp003017.4: The nobleman paid. And paid. And paid. He sold his weapons and armor and art until, finally, he took his own life. "You are a useful girl," chuckled the peddler as the doll returned to him.
weapon.story.wp003018.1: "I saw a girl," began the man. \n"She lay lifeless on the ground as countless black birds \npecked at her flesh."
weapon.story.wp003018.2: "I scooped up her feverish body and rushed away \nas fast as my legs could carry me."
weapon.story.wp003018.3: "The next thing I knew, her bloodied body stirred in \nmy arms and she began to breathe once more."
weapon.story.wp003018.4: "Ah, but there is one other part to this tale: \nI have told it to you backwards."
weapon.story.wp003019.1:
A remote village of outlaws lies deep within the mountains. 
One day, a young girl who became separated from 
her parents wanders in, 
causing the curious outlaws to sheathe their weapons.
weapon.story.wp003019.2:
The outlaws quickly take to the girl and begin doting on her. 
They give her food. They give her blankets. They give her 
flowers. Her charm completely cleanses 
their cold and savage hearts.
weapon.story.wp003019.3:
Eventually, the girl asks to go home. But the outlaws now 
consider themselves her parents, and so lock her in a cage. 
She pleads with them to leave with her, 
but they do not listen.
weapon.story.wp003019.4:
One day, the village is attacked by a massive bear that 
slaughters everyone save for the girl behind the thick bars of 
her cage. As she sits among the blood and 
flesh, she whispers "I told you so."
weapon.story.wp003020.1:
There was once a cowardly monster. 
Though bigger than all the rest of the monsters, 
he was still afraid of everything, and his friends 
made endless fun of him because of it.
weapon.story.wp003020.2:
The monster was afraid because he knew his power 
was the greatest, and he worried he might accidentally 
kill one of his friends. This is why he always 
stayed very quiet and kept to himself.
weapon.story.wp003020.3: True strength is not wielding great power, the monster often thought. True strength is being able to stand tall and protect your friends.
weapon.story.wp003020.4:
But his friends didn't know that, so they kept 
disparaging him for being weak. A coward. 
A big ol' scaredy-cat. But oddly enough, the monster 
always had an endless amount of friends around him.
weapon.story.wp003021.1:
The royals have lost their minds,
rounding up the nation's blacksmiths for something like this.
I have my pride—I won't just grit my teeth and
do as I'm told. I do this job because
I want to protect people.
weapon.story.wp003021.2:
Seems like some of the other blacksmiths were
won over with cash. Not me, though.
Some things in life matter more than money,
and I won't become their pet no matter how much they offer.
Hurry up and set me free!
weapon.story.wp003021.3:
I take back everything I said.
I'll do whatever you ask, so please, just don't hurt my family.
That said, my job is to smash hammer
against metal—I've never swung a hammer at a person before.
weapon.story.wp003021.4:
Eventually I was let go, and the "reward" they gave me for
assisting with their experiment was what
remained of my family after they had been torn apart by
smiths like myself and then stitched back together by machines.
weapon.story.wp003022.1: One day when I was little, my mother was driving me along this\ncoastline I've never been to before. I kept quiet because \nbecause she had this look on her face that kind of scared me.
weapon.story.wp003022.2: Once we arrived to a cape, she suddenly broke down on me \ncrying "I'm sorry". As a child it was my first time seeing my\nmother like that and I was just confused.
weapon.story.wp003022.3: I asked her, "Why are you crying?". Then without answering\nme she just hit the gas and we took off towards the cliff.\nI couldn't clearly remember what happened from there on.
weapon.story.wp003022.4: I was the only one saved. Even now I could still hear her\ncalling me whenever I get close to an ocean. Why did she\nwanted to die? I just don't know.
weapon.story.wp003023.1:
There was once a land ruled by a dragon. 
Once a year, a girl was sent off under the pretense of 
slaying it, even though all knew she would fail. 
This sacrifice, however, ensured peace.
weapon.story.wp003023.2:
Each year, they armed a girl with a dingy sword unbefitting 
a maiden's disposition and told her to never let it go, 
for it was a weapon with which 
she might slay their mighty adversary.
weapon.story.wp003023.3:
Every year, a girl valiantly faced the dragon, 
attempting to believe in herself 
and her blade. And every year, 
the dragon easily swallowed her whole.
weapon.story.wp003023.4:
But the last time this happened, 
the dragon perished; toxins in the ore used to 
forge the blade finally fell the beast. 
Sadly, none remain to remember the bravery of the girls.
weapon.story.wp003024.1:
We're finally going camping tomorrow! My bag is packed and ready
to go, and I'm so excited I can hardly sleep! We leave
first thing in the morning—oh geez, I hope I'm not late!
weapon.story.wp003024.2:
Camping day is finally here, so we met in the plaza and left
together! Our campsite is in a dumping ground past the
four mountains. There's ten of us plus the teacher—
it's gonna be so fun!
weapon.story.wp003024.3:
Four of our group got lost, but seven got to the city safe and
sound! Once we set up camp, we can finally go hunting.
I'm gonna be the best hunter—I won't lose to anyone!
weapon.story.wp003024.4:
The teacher got shot in the head! My stomach's ripped apart!
When the muzzle flashes, my friends go flying! But I'm not scared,
'cause battle hypnosis is great! Best camping trip ever
yaaaay!
weapon.story.wp003025.1: My brother was a valiant soldier who met a glorious end\nand is now revered as our nation's guard. But when I joined up,\nI found not a warrior's end, but the inside of a field hospital.
weapon.story.wp003025.2:
As soldiers died around me, I overhead an officer:
"These poor kids—these have-nots—throw their lives away for
a chance at glory. When they die, we name them gods, which
just brings more to the fight."
weapon.story.wp003025.3:
I hated the enemy for killing my brother. I hated my country
for sending young, poor people like my brother into battle. I hated
the world. And the next thing I knew, I was holding a greatsword.
weapon.story.wp003025.4:
My killing of the officer was forgiven because of my
military exploits. I returned home a hero. But as the leaders
were giving me a medal, I gripped my greatsword and 
swore revenge on them all.
weapon.story.wp003027.1:
Once, a noble samurai served a feudal lord.
In the beginning, he respected his idealistic lord and carried
out his will. But as time passed, the lord grew tyrannical, so the
samurai left his service.
weapon.story.wp003027.2:
The samurai made his way to a temple in the mountains
said to house a blade that could smite evil. After receiving it,
he gathered like-minded warriors at the temple to take down
the evil lord.
weapon.story.wp003027.3:
The samurai set out with the warriors. But the lord had a great
army, and a fierce battle soon erupted. "So long as we have this
blade, we cannot lose!" cried the samurai. 
"Come! We fight for our future!"
weapon.story.wp003027.4:
The samurai lay in a river of blood, the blade impaled in his
chest. Some said the weapon slew him for betraying his lord,
others for sacrificing his companions. As for the lord, he only
laughed.
weapon.story.wp003028.1:
There was once a man who dreamt of going to space, and
he eventually managed to save enough for a journey.
As his family saw him off to the spaceship,
he looked to be the happiest man in the world.
weapon.story.wp003028.2:
Yet there was a defect in the spaceship, and he was barely
able to strap himself into an escape pod before it exploded.
Eventually, the pod landed in the ocean
and drifted to a small deserted island.
weapon.story.wp003028.3: He used tools from the pod to make a hut, and also to hunt\nanimals for food. Then he began working on a board from\nthe pod, turning it into a magnificent wooden oar.
weapon.story.wp003028.4:
When the man returned, he expected a reunion with his family.
But his wife had thought him dead and remarried,
and his child no longer remembered his face.
All he had left was the oar that saved his life.
weapon.story.wp003029.1:
Long ago, there was a general and a loyal samurai.
Though of different backgrounds, they were fierce friends.
But one day, the general dreamed of glory and entered battle
only to be gravely injured.
weapon.story.wp003029.2:
The general saw only the enemy, the rain, and the corpses of
his men. Just as he thought he might perish, the samurai rose
from the corpse heap and used his remaining strength to
protect his friend.
weapon.story.wp003029.3:
Afterward, the general became a lord and gave the family of
his deceased friend a coveted position in his own clan. Alas,
that was the beginnings of our current lord and his terrifying
lapdogs.
weapon.story.wp003029.4:
The will to give all for a friend? The loyalty of a family who
took up the position? All faded in time. All became chaos.
Had the significance of this family stayed as it once was,
perhaps I...
weapon.story.wp003030.1: I'm sorry he hasn't come back yet, someone told me today.\nIt's true, I met him here long, long ago. We fell madly in love, and\nnow he's just...gone.
weapon.story.wp003030.2: Forget him and find a new man, someone told me today.\nBut I would never do such a thing. He is the only one for me, and\nI would rather die than be with another.
weapon.story.wp003030.3: He found a new girl somewhere else, someone told me today.\nOf course he did—such wanderings are nothing new. But things\nare different this time, because I know he loves me.
weapon.story.wp003030.4: There's a cage outside town that no one knows about. My beloved\nsits inside. Everyone thinks he left, but he has always been here.\nI love you, darling, and I will never let you leave. Never.
weapon.story.wp003031.1:
No matter how science advances—no matter how the magic of
fairy tales becomes reality—
humans will find ways to kill one another.
This is why I once again find myself standing on a battlefield.
weapon.story.wp003031.2:
I've been here for years, all for my family.
But my current salary still might not be enough to pay for
my child's upbringing.
weapon.story.wp003031.3:
All I can do is kill.
Yet I need not fear death in battle with this body.
weapon.story.wp003031.4:
For you see, if this imitation of a body fails,
I simply exchange it for the next one.
Yes, our replaceable bodies allow us to keep killing one another
even after physical death.
weapon.story.wp003032.1:
Can't stick with the boss anymore.
Sneaking into the Thieves' Graveyard?
He's mad! We've been through a lot over the years,
but this is a step too far, even for me.
weapon.story.wp003032.2:
Things fell apart on the way home after escaping the Graveyard.
It was the kid's fault, of course—he treats us like dogs.
Worst part is that he's more
talented than any of us and we know it.
weapon.story.wp003032.3:
Everyone knows who he is: He leads the nation's best thieves
guild and takes everything he wants. The way he acts...
The way he steals...
Every thief in the land wants to be just like him.
weapon.story.wp003032.4:
Finally saw the kid in town. Was relieved to see him alive,
but shocked at how different he was.
What happened to his bejeweled clothes? His sharp gaze?
Did he get a girl? Oh, my brother...
weapon.story.wp003033.1:
Can't stick with the boss anymore.
Sneaking into the Thieves' Graveyard?
He's mad! We've been through a lot over the years,
but this is a step too far, even for me.
weapon.story.wp003033.2:
Things fell apart on the way home after escaping the Graveyard.
It was the kid's fault, of course—he treats us like dogs.
Worst part is that he's more
talented than any of us and we know it.
weapon.story.wp003033.3:
Everyone knows who he is: He leads the nation's best thieves
guild and takes everything he wants. The way he acts...
The way he steals...
Every thief in the land wants to be just like him.
weapon.story.wp003033.4:
Finally saw the kid in town. Was relieved to see him alive,
but shocked at how different he was.
What happened to his bejeweled clothes? His sharp gaze?
Did he get a girl? Oh, my brother...
weapon.story.wp003034.1:
Can't stick with the boss anymore.
Sneaking into the Thieves' Graveyard?
He's mad! We've been through a lot over the years,
but this is a step too far, even for me.
weapon.story.wp003034.2:
Things fell apart on the way home after escaping the Graveyard.
It was the kid's fault, of course—he treats us like dogs.
Worst part is that he's more
talented than any of us and we know it.

weapon.story.wp003037.1: There is a plant that continues to grow in chaos.\nMy job is to keep it pruned,\nand my sweat serves as proof that I live.
weapon.story.wp003037.2: But people also grow in chaos,\nwhich means I must prune them as well.\nOnce again, I shower in sprays of blood.
weapon.story.wp003037.3: This sword has cut down both plant and man.\nThis blade has embraced my gentle and evanescent self.\nThis thin piece of steel is the only noble life in this place.
weapon.story.wp003037.4:
As an era came to an end, a greatsword was unearthed
—one wrapped in a bloody garment and a tangle of vines.
The black bird that perched beside it
stared at the dull glint of the blade.
weapon.story.wp003038.1:
Memories sometimes come back to me;
flavors of food we never ate together,
scenes from places to which we never ventured.
Each time, my heart aches from the nostalgia and sadness.

weapon.story.wp003039.1:
A lone man gazes over a heated city from atop his tower,
then unfolds himself onto the ground and begins to sing.
He loves the sight before him,
for he is the young king of this fine land.
weapon.story.wp003039.2: When the hair of manhood is upon him, foreign soldiers attack.\nThe king does not know war, so he cradles his baby and flees.\nHis beloved subjects spill blood, ready to fight to the death.
weapon.story.wp003039.3: The king learns people cannot be saved by love alone. Tearfully,\nhe leaves his country and crosses the sea to seek his fortune,\nhis surviving daughter is all he has left in the world.
weapon.story.wp003039.4:
When the king's back is bent from age,
he finds himself surrounded by loved ones:
a new wife, a new country,
new subjects. But his beloved daughter is nowhere to be found.
weapon.story.wp003040.1:
In a distant past, a princess came to an army on the verge
of annihilation and brought them victory after victory.
She became an object of worship, but was then
crucified as a criminal after a defeat.
weapon.story.wp003040.2: In a distant place, a girl made a living slaughtering\nevil rulers so she might avenge the weak.\nBut one fell day, the daughter of a lord did the same for her.
weapon.story.wp003040.3:
In a distant future, a nurse will be admired as the white angel,
freeing countless numbers from their pain.
But when she goes against the morals of her world,
she will be assassinated.
weapon.story.wp003040.4:
In a distant storybook world,
a girl prayed for her master to recover, caring
not if it cost her innocent life. She paid no heed to how
her justice warped and sickened in the process.
weapon.story.wp003041.1:
Once there was a special establishment,
open only on New Year's Day, whose sole purpose was to
sever relationships. The village women gossiped
that it could help a person end old, bad ties.
weapon.story.wp003041.2: One woman heard the rumor and took her good-for-nothing,\ngambling husband to the place, hoping to be free of him at last.\nWith resolve in her heart, she knocked on the door.
weapon.story.wp003041.3:
The door opened to reveal a beautiful woman with a katana
as large as the wielder. The husband ogled her,
but once he realized he was there for the purpose of divorce,
his attitude changed.
weapon.story.wp003041.4:
As he thrashed about, the woman brought her blade down,
sending the husband's head sailing through the air and severing
the relationship for good. When the wife saw the woman smile,
she screamed.
weapon.story.wp003042.1:
There was once a fishmonger who worked harder
than anyone else. One day, he sold a great catch to a royal
official and received his pay in an envelope.
Excited, he returned home to his mother.
weapon.story.wp003042.2:
As his ill mother lay abed, he counted the money in the envelope.
But the amount was not as much as he was expecting,
and when he finished, he was no longer
certain that he could afford her medicine.
weapon.story.wp003042.3:
His income lessened as time went on, and he grew
increasingly weak. One day, the official summoned him:
A thief had stolen from a rice dealer,
and blame had been pinned on the fishmonger.
weapon.story.wp003042.4: The fishmonger, of course, had stolen no rice.\nBut he accepted the blame with a smile,\npleased that he no longer had to look after his mother.
weapon.story.wp003043.1:
The blade is sleek and black, yet seems to give off light.
Its beauty remains untarnished even after testing it
on my servants, which makes it a personal favorite.
Alas, it has been stolen by a thief.
weapon.story.wp003043.2:
The scoundrel who stole my treasure is well-known in low
corners of the city. He's said to have a young face,
as well as a small frame that makes him an adept thief.
Just the thought of him makes me rage.
weapon.story.wp003043.3:
I search the city and find him gliding silently through the streets.
My treasure dances in his hands,
plunging into the bodies of his foes.
Shaking with anger, I suddenly leap before him.
weapon.story.wp003043.4:
Cut me down! I cry. The blade's black sheen is so much
more lovely that when I wield it, and I feel a great desire to
witness it up close.
Yet the thief scoffs at me and refuses to grant my wish.
weapon.story.wp003044.1: We are tailors.\nCome to us if you desire to wear a masterpiece!
weapon.story.wp003044.2: We will make anything to suit your body, your mind,\nand your heart. A bespoke article of stunning\nbeauty lovingly created just for you.
weapon.story.wp003044.3: We will grant you blissful memories that bring you\nto a peaceful death. We will grant you hateful memories\nthat give you the strength to survive the morrow.
weapon.story.wp003044.4:
Oh, what a busy day it's been! People cannot
live without one reason or another, but it's so hard
coming up with false lives... Oh, a customer!
What sort of memories are you looking for today?
weapon.story.wp003045.1:
Bloody Thirteenth Month:
The calendar means little now.
This cursed year will continue into eternity until
we complete our mission or someone shows their true colors.
weapon.story.wp003045.2:
People started going missing that year, most related to the
military. The government searched high and low for the
culprit, but by the time December rolled around,
twenty-three people were gone.
weapon.story.wp003045.3: No one felt like ringing in the new year—and when January came, they found the corpses of all the missing people in the bakery basement. It was an abattoir. A midden heap. A horror.
weapon.story.wp003045.4:
The atrocity was carried out by villagers whose families
were taken as decoys for military operations.
The government had no idea they were all in on it,
and the villagers conspired well to make their stories match.
weapon.story.wp003046.1:
A man with a massive sword showed up in town not long ago.
The look in his eyes isn't...normal. Is he a powerful mercenary?
A fugitive? Either way,
he's clearly a bad dude we should stay far away from.
weapon.story.wp003046.2: Every day, the bad dude nurses a drink in the tavern.\nHe's quiet, but he'll say a word here and there if you talk to him.\nHe once told me that each scar on his body is a victory in battle.
weapon.story.wp003046.3:
I learned why the bad dude is scary:
He's been in over a hundred battles!
He cuts down enemies in one blow, and is nicknamed the Iron
Reaper. He's like the protagonist of some grand tale.
weapon.story.wp003046.4:
The bad dude was a total fraud! The battle scars?
He was actually run over by a carriage. The sword?
He took it from a dead mercenary—no idea how to even swing it.
Talk about disappointing!
weapon.story.wp003047.1:
Strength is everything in this world; wealth and renown is given
only to the powerful. I was unrivaled since the day
I received my axe, and all who
saw me quickly bent the knee.
weapon.story.wp003047.2:
Land, coin, food, partners—it was all mine. People envied me,
of course. Some even attacked. But when they did,
my axe put them in their place. Still,
I never wished for this. I just wanted to be loved.
weapon.story.wp003047.3:
Eventually I was blessed with a child, and all the villagers
cheered. The man who became my husband came to
love me, and that is when I
understood what it meant to be fulfilled.
weapon.story.wp003047.4:
But I failed in birth. Though the axe was at my side,
I lacked the strength to fight the child that eventually
killed me. If I am ever born again,
I will seek my child out and have revenge.
weapon.story.wp003048.1: Flowers bloom when she smiles.\nHer joy spreads vitality.\nBuds bloom as she does.
weapon.story.wp003048.2: Birds sing when she sends word.\nThey lend their wings as she speaks to us.
weapon.story.wp003048.3: The wind howls as she despairs.\nThe heavens rage as she weeps for our tragedies.
weapon.story.wp003048.4: The moon shines when she comes to us.\nShe leads our human sacrifices away as we sleep.
weapon.story.wp003049.1: The boy dreams of a djinn. The djinn offers him clean water,\nripe fruits⁠—anything he wants. In his dreams,\nhe eats his fill and greets every morning in high spirits.
weapon.story.wp003049.2: The lady dreams of a djinn. "I saw a beautiful man on the\nstreet this morning! Bring him to me!" The djinn searches\nthe city in tears before finally making her wish come true.
weapon.story.wp003049.3: The king dreams of the djinn. He drowns in a sea of corpses;\nhe is so weary of killing. The djinn gently extends a hand,\npulling him into a soft embrace.
weapon.story.wp003049.4:
The djinn gives people dreams that will never come true.
But the least they can do is give them what they
struggle so hard to attain—and what slips
from their fingers amidst their reverie.
weapon.story.wp003051.1: Once, there was a village that suffered from a dragon. Stalwart\nmen attempted to drive the beast hence, but its flames reduced\nall who came near to ash.
weapon.story.wp003051.2:
The village was on the edge of destruction when the people heard
rumors of a man who wielded a mighty greatsword. His weapon was
said to hold the power of flame, and had been used to slay
countless fiends.
weapon.story.wp003051.3:
The villagers tracked down the swordsman and begged him for
succor, for they hoped his sword could stand against the dragon's
flame. And though they knew it was a heavy request, the man
quickly and confidently agreed.
weapon.story.wp003051.4: As they hoped, the greatsword resisted the dragon's flame.\nBut the swordsman, alas, did not—instead turning into ashes on\nthe wind and vanishing without a trace.
weapon.story.wp003052.1: Once, there was a curious wind spirit who sought to befriend a\nhuman girl. But the spirit could not speak, so it tried to think of\nother ways to communicate.
weapon.story.wp003052.2: First, it made a breeze. The girl's skirt fluttered, causing her\nto frolic and laugh merrily—which only made the spirit want to\nplay with her all the more.
weapon.story.wp003052.3: Next, it created a blast of wind. Trees bent double, and the girl\nshut herself inside to weather the storm. What could the spirit\ndo to make her come out?
weapon.story.wp003052.4: Finally, it created a tornado that knocked down the house—\nbut alas, it also blew the girl clean away, killing her.\n...Oh dear. Perhaps that was a bit too much.
weapon.story.wp003053.1: A cursed greatsword was enshrined in a cave off the coast.\nWhen a reckless man found it and reached for its hilt, a strange\nvoice called out.
weapon.story.wp003053.2: Next thing he knew, he was surrounded by the ghosts of people\nwho had died in battle, all with the same question on their\nlips: "What is the point in fighting?"
weapon.story.wp003053.3: But he could not remember why he fought. Why he had come. What\nwas he even doing there.
weapon.story.wp003053.4:
The dead took his hand and led him further into the cave,
until he came across a clear spring that emanated with a soft
blue glow. And when he set foot into the spring, he fell down,
down, down into that glorious light.
weapon.story.wp003054.1:
Legends tell of a time long, long ago when the god of
light created six weapons and scattered them across the world.
One, a greatsword that heightened one's will to live, was at
the peak of a mountain where none survived to claim it.
weapon.story.wp003054.2:
One day, a noble-minded knight attempted the peak. As he got
closer, he found countless corpses of adventurers who had
come before, still pristine from the cold. He politely buried them all
before finally arriving at the peak.
weapon.story.wp003054.3:
There he found a greatsword emitting a warm light, but the poor
knight scarcely had any energy left; his rations were gone,
and he had not eaten for ten days. As he reached for the sword,
he knew he would soon perish in this place.
weapon.story.wp003054.4:
The moment he took sword in hand, power raced through him and
he wanted to live. To eat. He could eat anything now.
No—he wanted to eat. He had to eat. So the knight climbed quickly
down the mountain to undo the graves he had made.
weapon.story.wp003055.1: The girl sat alone in a dark cell for many a year. It was\na darkness that sapped all sense of time, so she simply\nwaited for each moment to pass.
weapon.story.wp003055.2:
The only time she saw light is when she was given food. Her door
would open a crack, and a blinding ray would come streaming into
the room. She lived for these moments; indeed, they were all that
gave her life meaning.
weapon.story.wp003055.3:
She wolfed down her food and resumed waiting for the light.
That was her life; she knew nothing else. But one day, a man
appeared who had learned of the girl's plight and felt great
sympathy for her.
weapon.story.wp003055.4:
He opened the door and extended his hand to her, at which
point she promptly bit it off. She proceeded to eat every
last scrap of the man, then folded her legs beneath her and
resumed her vigil for the light.
weapon.story.wp003056.1:
There was once a swordsman unmatched in ability.
He served no lord. Taught no students⁠. Accepted no salary
or honors. Instead, he took a single apprentice
and walked the land in search of justice.
weapon.story.wp003056.2:
They stopped to help any in need, cutting down evil when they
saw it. But though countless were saved by their
journey of righteousness, the seed of evil had
begun to grow right under the swordsman's nose.
weapon.story.wp003056.3:
Having seen evil in all its forms, the apprentice fomented
rebellion to change the world at the core.
The swordsman was blamed and exiled,
his beloved weapon replaced by a blunted blade.
weapon.story.wp003056.4:
The former apprentice killed until his life was taken by a samurai
his old master met in a faraway land and taught his skills to
before passing. Yet none know the weapon the samurai
claimed as a reward was the old swordsman's beloved blade.
weapon.story.wp003057.1: He put his plan in motion that day, the knife trembling in his small hand. I killed the captain. I wanted to save the girl he was abusing so we could flee together. I dreamed of that moment.
weapon.story.wp003057.2:
The ■■■■ rocked violently in the storm as men worked
desperately to keep it intact. I slipped past them
toward the bow of the ship. Toward the ■■■■■■■.
Then I plunged the ■■■■■ into him.
weapon.story.wp003057.3:
The storm washed the ■■■■■ away.
I'd ■■■■ed the ■■■■■■■, but the girl's ■■■■■■
was broken. Nothing ■■■■■■■■ now.
And as desp■■■■■■■ claimed me, a black bird appeared.
weapon.story.wp003057.4: The black bird glared at ■■ th■■■■h the rain, ■■■■■■■■ me\nback to ■■■■■■■. I c■■■■n't l■t t■■■ be ■■e end. I ■■d\nt■ ■■■ o■t of h■■■—I had to ■■■■■■■.
weapon.story.wp003058.1:
I love you I love you I love you

The trembling of my body instantly
stops when you fight by my side
weapon.story.wp003058.2:
I love you I love you I love you

Your warmth soothes the grief
I carry for the child I lost
weapon.story.wp003058.3:
I love you I love you I love you

The whole of your life nourishes
my newly blossoming heart
weapon.story.wp003058.4:
I love you I love you I love you

The many years I spent with you
keep me ruthless and cruel
weapon.story.wp003059.1:
Humanity once had the concept of "friendship." It is said to
be a reason why old humans were social animals.
It also served to increase the survivability of
individuals by acting as a group.
weapon.story.wp003059.2: Humanity once had the concept of "love." This let one choose\na mate in an environment free from evolutionary danger,\nbut proved inefficient in terms of preserving the species.
weapon.story.wp003059.3:
Humanity once had the concept of "family," where
groups related by blood (or sometimes not) formed
communities. Some relied on the supervision of "parents"
(or elders), which at times made things much worse.
weapon.story.wp003059.4: Humanity once had the concept of "self," which led to a diverse \nspecies. But those with minority personalities naturally died out, \nleaving only one dominant "self" in the present world.
weapon.story.wp003060.1:
"Say there! Mind if I borrow that monster of yours?"
"Why?"
"There's something I want to test with its claws.
Please! Just for one day!"
weapon.story.wp003060.2:
"Mind if I keep your monster for another day?"
"Why?"
"Well, it's taking a while to wipe the blood off.
But I'll give it back squeaky clean! I promise!"
weapon.story.wp003060.3:
"HELP ME, MASTER! I'M GOING TO DIE!"
"Why?"
"SHE'S MAKING ME USE MY POWER FOR
HORRIBLE THINGS⁠!"
weapon.story.wp003060.4: "You can have your monster back; I don't need it anymore.\nSee, 'cause I made sure to get rid of all the pesky\ngirls that crowd around you. And nOw...YoU aRE MInE."
weapon.story.wp003061.1: I amassed a collection of beautiful treasures\nfrom all across the world.\nHe stole all of them away with exquisite skill.
weapon.story.wp003061.2: And so I bought more treasures. But this time,\nI spent an equal amount on security measures.
weapon.story.wp003061.3: And yet, like a breeze or a flickering shadow,\nhe managed to slip through my security and\nsteal the treasures again.
weapon.story.wp003061.4: I amassed a collection of beautiful treasures from\nall across the world. And beholding his exquisite skills\nin thievery made it all worthwhile.
weapon.story.wp003062.1:
Look, xxxxx is REAL!
And no, it's NOT Mom or Dad.
xxxxx is real and only visits sweet and adorable kids like ME.
See? I even got TWO presents this year!
weapon.story.wp003062.2:
Who believes in xxxxx at this age?
Me. I do.
Even after Mom and Dad came clean,
I'd still find a present by my pillow in the morning.
weapon.story.wp003062.3:
Tell me the truth, my darling husband.
You've been my xxxxx for me and me alone, yes?
Wait, what do you mean, no? We grew up together!
You lived next door! You're the only one who could've...
Then who gave me this present?
weapon.story.wp003062.4: xxxxx did, in fact, give me what I wanted each year. And what I wanted this year was the truth. Who're you? Wait, is this a photo? THAT'S you? Ugh! Gross! You've got to be kidding me. I was better off not knowing!
weapon.story.wp003063.1:
There was once a forest on an eastern island, and there lived a
creature with the body of a human but the head and wings of a bird.
It was called Karasu Tengu, and the people hated it.
But the Karasu Tengu wanted friends badly.
weapon.story.wp003063.2:
A traveler wandered lost into the Karasu Tengu's forest,
weary and on the verge of starvation.
The Karasu Tengu hesitantly offered its aid—perhaps
that would be an acceptable way of interacting with a human.
weapon.story.wp003063.3:
The Karasu Tengu made its first friend.
The traveler did not fear it, and told many tales of their travels.
But not wanting to part with its friend, the Karasu Tengu cast
a spell and transformed the traveler into a Karasu Tengu!
weapon.story.wp003063.4:
The traveler was delighted—they could fly anywhere.
"They will throw stones at you," the Karasu Tengu warned.
But the traveler descended upon the town, laughing merrily with
the townsfolk. The Karasu Tengu unsheathed its sword...
weapon.story.wp003065.1:
The girl did not understand the meaning of being born.
She found herself here one day, a puppet to her house.
As she hid her pain, everyone around her used her
to their own ends.
weapon.story.wp003065.2:
When she saw the woman, she immediately knew that this woman
would bring about her death. She'd never seen anyone so beautiful.
How cold she was in her slaughter...
Perhaps there were worse ways to die.
weapon.story.wp003065.3:
And yet, the woman listened to the girl as she cursed the world that
bent her to its whims, and instead wielded her blade to help the girl.
The rainy day when she was drenched in the woman's blood was
the true day of her birth.
weapon.story.wp003065.4:
The two live together peacefully and uneventfully,
but each day reminds the girl that she is, in fact, alive.
But little does she know that the woman,
too, was reborn on the day they met...
weapon.story.wp003066.1:
(A Blacksmith's Work Journal) Gettin' a request from a client,
I take up my trusty hammer and forge a metal gooreatsword.
It's good for takin' out metal monsters, or so I hear.
I'm but a humble smith, but I've always dreamed of adventure...
weapon.story.wp003066.2:
(A Blacksmith's Travelogue: 1) Gooreatsword in hand,
I've come to a dungeon I heard about from an adventurer.
There's apparently tons of metal monsters around here...
I even saw one, but it got away from me. The thing was crazy fast!
weapon.story.wp003066.3:
(A Blacksmith's Travelogue: 2) Who's the wise guy who said
this weapon could take down metal critters? They run away
too quick! Been fightin' weaker fellas in the meantime, but
I can't swing this sword like I can my hammer. It's just too heavy.
weapon.story.wp003066.4:
(A Blacksmith's Travelogue: 3) I run into a metal slime,
swing my sword, and...critical hit! Level up! But you know what?
I figured out what I really want to do. Can't wait to
get back to the guild and pick up my hammer again.
weapon.story.wp003067.1:
ENTRY NO. 1
I've been put in charge of researching weapons called
"relics," but the things negate everything we know
about science. How am I supposed to study 'em?
weapon.story.wp003067.2:
ENTRY NO. 2
Modern weapons? Fine. But I've never seen an outdated
weapon like this. And just because it's old doesn't mean
I can't feel the chill coming off it.
weapon.story.wp003067.3:
ENTRY NO. 13
Just how many people have been killed by this weapon?
The chill I feel from it makes it seem cursed...
I wonder what its previous owners thought when they wielded it?
weapon.story.wp003067.4:
REPORT 0001
I've been ordered to study a weapon found in the ruins.
But from what I can tell from the notes that
accompany it, I'm better off not touching it.
weapon.story.wp003068.1:
One morning, in a deep and dark enchanted wood,
a great dark sword lay on the ground.
Who could have left it here?
Alas, the insects that awaken with the morning sun know nothing.
weapon.story.wp003068.2: As the sun rises and the insects finish their meal,\nthey ask the critters of the wood who could have left the sword.\nAlas, they playful little critters know nothing.
weapon.story.wp003068.3:
As the sun sets and the critters return to their nests,
they ask the proud beasts who prowl the wood at night who
could have left the sword. Alas, the beasts, searching for mates,
know nothing.
weapon.story.wp003068.4:
As the moon sets and the beasts slumber—
and before the insects wake once again—
the never-sleeping black birds see.
They know the weapon is what became of a ■■■■.
weapon.story.wp003069.1:
It was supposed to be a simple mission—
a quick patrol around the block. 
But when the enemy shot us down on a desert island, the other
four survivors and I began a heroic struggle against all odds!
weapon.story.wp003069.2:
The nerd built weapons out of the fallen units.
Pretty flimsy things if I'm being honest, but hey,
beggars and horses and wishes and all that.
I'm good as long as I have my arms.
weapon.story.wp003069.3:
Captain was killed in battle. Beheaded. He wasn't super
reliable, but he also wasn't a bad guy, so I'll try to
avenge him. This won't kill my will to fight—if anything,
it only steels my conviction!
weapon.story.wp003069.4:
I felled thousands of enemies. Thousands!
Though my sword was just a hunk of metal, my arm never
strained under the weight. It feels light as... Wait,
I can't even tell if it's light anymore.
weapon.story.wp003070.2: Forgot your password?\nEnter your email to reset your password.\n__________

weapon.story.wp003102.1: The last drop of water will soon be lost to the blazing sun.\nEveryone knew it was coming to this, but we did nothing. Instead,\nwe let inaction eat away at our hearts.
weapon.story.wp003102.2:
This camp is a forsaken place, and people who take refuge here
have no other choice. I gave the last of my water to a child
earlier—her vacant eyes seemed to moisten just a bit as she
drank it down.
weapon.story.wp003102.3:
Those who die in war don't get a happy ending; they just perish in
misery, their final wishes forgotten. What would a god of this
world even look like? What expression would be on His face as
He watches us?
weapon.story.wp003102.4:
My time as an observer ends when I take up a sword. Do people
see me as a reaper as they surrender their lives to me without
resistance? With a blank expression, I swing one last time and
finish my task.
weapon.story.wp003103.1: Blue is the color of spring; of budding life.\nBlue is the color of seas; of overflowing life.\nBlue is the color of life—but it is an ignorant color.
weapon.story.wp003103.2: Red is the color of summer; of blazing flame.\nRed is the color of blood; of flooding vitality.\nRed is the color of life—but it is a lost color.
weapon.story.wp003103.3: White is the color of autumn; of rich abundance.\nWhite is the color of mist; of impeding boundaries.\nWhite is the color of life—but it is an innocent color.
weapon.story.wp003103.4: Black is the color of winter; of death and the end.\nBlack is the color of sin; of the defiling of existence.\nBlack is the color of life—the fate of everything.
weapon.story.wp003104.1:
Once, a titan appeared at a remote village on the verge of
collapse. Seeing that the people faced certain death,
the kindly titan dug up the earth, forming a river and
saving the village.
weapon.story.wp003104.2: Would you bring wood so we might have houses, Titan?\nThe titan effortlessly carried the timber to the village,\nand had the little houses built in no time flat.
weapon.story.wp003104.3: The wolves we hear at night frighten us greatly, Titan. The titan\nfollowed the howls and found the wolves' den, where he snuffed\nout the lives of every last one.
weapon.story.wp003104.4:
You're amazing, Titan! I want to be like you someday! With a
wide smile, the titan picked up the person who made this request,
squashed them flat, and stretched out the remains so they would
be just the right size.
weapon.story.wp003106.1: Once, a swordsman discovered a special ore deep in a cave.\nHe knew it held a great power, and brought it to an engineer\nso he might craft a greatsword with it.
weapon.story.wp003106.2: The blade was large and heavy, and too blunt to cut even paper.\nBut it was sturdy and never chipped, so the swordsman slowly\ngained renown for the way he battered foes to death.
weapon.story.wp003106.3: The swordsman's country called him a hero and awarded him a\nmedal. They also planned to reward the engineer, but that man had\nmixed feelings about his prize.
weapon.story.wp003106.4: "The ore is magical," said the engineer.\n"But if one does not possess the ability to use magic,\nmy weapon is little more than a crude bludgeon."
weapon.story.wp003107.1:
Why did this happen to me? I'm just a damn engineer! This war
took everything. My wife—my pregnant wife? I don't even know
if she's alive. All I have now is revenge, which is why
I devoted myself to weapon development.
weapon.story.wp003107.2:
My goal was to create living weapons. Weapons that thought.
Learned. Evolved. I would use them to inflict pain on the people
who took everything from me, but first I needed actual people to
serve as my materials.
weapon.story.wp003107.3:
I found children who had lost everything and altered them.
One by one, they were reborn as weapons. They, too, have surely
lost things precious to them, and I know that together, we will
turn our hate into power.
weapon.story.wp003107.4:
But when the work was done, I found a necklace that belonged to
my wife. A groan escaped my lips as I saw it, but my weapons made
no response. Once I had collected myself, I ordered one of
them to kill me.
weapon.story.wp003108.1:
His greatsword was the embodiment of our nation's justice.
He returned safely from any battlefield; he was a hero to the
people, and moreso to us soldiers. But one day, he vanished—and
now I am looking for him.
weapon.story.wp003108.2:
As I searched, I encountered plenty of rumors. And while some had
the ring of truth, I did not want to believe them— because the
man in those tales was an entirely different person from the hero
we all knew.
weapon.story.wp003108.3:
Sadly, the rumors turned out to be true: Our hero was now
wandering the land killing people indiscriminately. Would I be
able to kill him for his crimes? After all, this man had led me.
Saved me. Loved me.
weapon.story.wp003108.4:
I found him in the ruins of a church. When I asked why, he said
he killed in the name of justice. As the dust on the floor began
turning black with my blood, he whispered,
"I will enact justice until my last breath."
weapon.story.wp003111.1:
There was once a soldier who wielded a greatsword for a
war-loving king. He fought day after day, year after year,
and loved every moment of it, gaining great wealth and
fame as a result.
weapon.story.wp003111.2: The only thing he loved more than battle was climbing the castle\nwalls and looking down at the city, for he loathed the common folk.\nThat was why he gave all to the service of his king.
weapon.story.wp003111.3: After many battles, the man was named a general and summoned\nby the king. His heart sang as he walked to the throne room, for he\nknew his liege would have a great role for him in the next war.
weapon.story.wp003111.4:
But the king told the man the next war would be fought by
clockwork men and dismissed him. The next day, he leapt from the
wall and became a smudge on the ground that the common folk
simply ignored.
weapon.story.wp003112.1:
INSTRUCTIONS: PAGE 1
◆ Chop any part you like into pieces. Chop, chop, chop!
This will be easier if you take a really big swing,
but watch out for all the blood!
weapon.story.wp003112.2:
INSTRUCTIONS: PAGE 2
◆ Use the weight of the sword to crush stuff!
Beating the body to a pulp will bring great mental anguish
to the subject. Be sure the affected part doesn't fester.
weapon.story.wp003112.3:
INSTRUCTIONS: PAGE 3
◆ Apply pressure by squeezing between the ends of the blades!
The subject's head is perfect for this. You can adjust the
pressure with the handle, but be careful not to go too far!
weapon.story.wp003112.4:
INSTRUCTIONS: PAGE 4
◆ It's...blank. Looks like I'll be the fourth person to
be punished with this sword. I think they're testing out
methods, one person at a time? How have I ma—
weapon.story.wp003113.1: There was once a vile military unit called the Red Devils.\nThey were a terrifying bunch, made up of the most heinous criminals\nin the world. They were sent into battle for a single reason: to kill.
weapon.story.wp003113.2: One member of the force was larger and stronger than all the rest.\nHe wielded a fearsome rod, and laughed loudly as he used it to\nbreak apart buildings and people alike.
weapon.story.wp003113.3:
The man's father had taught him to let go and laugh when he was
having fun, so he did just that. He never recognized his acts as
a crime, because he was simply enjoying himself. It had been
this way since the day his parents died.
weapon.story.wp003113.4:
Driven to madness at the discovery of his wife's affair, his
father sat beside her corpse and laughed until his throat was raw.
The boy could not understand; he could only imitate his father
and how much he enjoyed himself.
weapon.story.wp003114.1:
An order of knights once served a royal family. Its captain was
so skilled with a sword, he could take on any number of enemies
and emerge victorious. People called him "The Iron Mask" for
the helm he always wore.
weapon.story.wp003114.2: In truth, however, the king had ordered the captain to never\nremove his helm. And while he obeyed his liege, no one else in\nthe order knew about his command.
weapon.story.wp003114.3:
Though few noticed, the king actually hated the captain.
But as he lacked the skill to defeat him, he instead forced
him to wear a cramped, uncomfortable iron helm that covered his
entire face.
weapon.story.wp003114.4:
The reason for this hate was petty indeed: The captain was a
handsome man, and the queen had grown infatuated with him.
And though that occurred decades ago, the king had never been
able to forgive him for it.
weapon.story.wp003116.1: "It's my fault he died. I have no right to call myself a knight."\nThe moment that thought came to me, a girl approached with a\nflock of blackbirds in tow.
weapon.story.wp003116.2: "Please help!" she cried. "Wicked men are chasing me!"\nWould saving her redeem me? I gripped the greatsword he left\nto me, took her hand, and ran.
weapon.story.wp003116.3:
"Give us the girl, unless you wish to die in her place!"
To surrender my life for another is no choice at all, and I was
reunited with him in heaven far more quickly than
I thought possible.
weapon.story.wp003116.4: "Good. That went well. Here's your money." You killed my father\nand claimed his sword: the only keepsake he left behind.\nIt is not yours to hold. Farewell.
weapon.story.wp003119.1: An Emperor must be a visionary. Though they may not come true,\nWe must not forget to dream. The people leave the future in Our\nhands precisely because We walk through endless ambition.
weapon.story.wp003119.2: An Emperor must be majestic. Others nations must know of Our\nauthority—and as the representative of Our country, We must not\nend up disregarded.
weapon.story.wp003119.3: An Emperor must be extravagant. Great wealth should\naccompany great power, for the people make an effort to learn\nprecisely because they admire Our position.
weapon.story.wp003119.4:
However, an Emperor must not be immortal. The world is
constantly changing, and one who seeks to take Our life will
eventually appear. But an Emperor must not fear the moment
of downfall.
weapon.story.wp003120.1:
There was once a mountain known as Mt. Nevermore, so called
because none who went there ever returned. Many legends surrounded
the place, such as tales of man-eating demons and hot springs that
could cure any illness.
weapon.story.wp003120.2: One day, a woman's husband went missing. When she searched\nhigh and low and found no trace, the other villages began\nwhispering about how he had been swallowed by Mt. Nevermore.
weapon.story.wp003120.3:
Grasping this faint ray of hope, the woman ventured onto the
mountain. As she walked deep into the dense forest, she eventually
stumbled across her husband collapsed in a pool of blood on
the ground.
weapon.story.wp003120.4: The woman was relieved; she had stabbed her husband, but he had\ngotten away. As she thought about if he had been trying to find\nthe hot spring, she heard something very large moving behind her.
weapon.story.wp003500.1:
You taught me to walk the path of carnage. No matter how
I wailed, you stared down at me, expression never changing.
Like the superhuman divine, your spirit was transcendent.
You were everything that caused my heart to stir.
weapon.story.wp003500.2:
You freed me from a world of captivity. As we lived our
quiet, peaceful lives, I would sometimes see on your face
the shadows of the burden you once bore. Though powerless,
I thought I could chase away your melancholy.
weapon.story.wp003500.3:
After you betrayed your house, you grew dull, the cold
clarity in your eyes fading away. Yet you cannot hide
it—you dance like a demon among countless blades.
If my blood could sharpen you, I would gladly offer my neck.
weapon.story.wp003500.4:
You gave me so many joyful days. It is because of your
immense strength that you do not know how to care for
yourself, is it not? Your life is surely beyond my comprehension,
but regardless, you are happiness embodied to me.
weapon.story.wp003501.1: "Understood." The word contains no emotion for me.\nI have said it hundreds of times.
weapon.story.wp003501.2: I am a puppet that obeys orders to kill. I snuff out emotions as\nI snuff out lives, and will do so until the day I rot away.
weapon.story.wp003501.3: The age we live in determined my station from the moment of\nmy birth—which is why I burn to at least live as myself.
weapon.story.wp003501.4: "Understood." The day I said that to the girl, I felt an\nexhilaration unlike anything that had ever come before.
weapon.story.wp003502.1:
Family was everything to me, and I considered 
it my sacred duty to protect my beloved wife and son. 
But the sudden appearance of a Flower snuffed 
out my son's life in the blink of an eye.
weapon.story.wp003502.2: People are closely managed in this world corrupted by the Flowers.\nWe're forced to fight so we might take our lives back—and though\nI am practically a prisoner, I gleefully wield my sword for revenge.
weapon.story.wp003502.3: We captives wipe out the Flowers. My wife and I survive the\nfight, and share our joy together. But in that moment,\nthe world stands still.
weapon.story.wp003502.4: That's when I remember how we are managed; that nothing is\nfree of binds in this world, not even emotion. And that it was people\nwho took my wife's life.
weapon.story.wp003503.1:
There was once an android soldier who did not fear death.
He wielded a great blade and wandered from battle to battle,
learning how to use his endless life by watching
others being stolen.
weapon.story.wp003503.2: One day, the soldier found a gorgeous red rose blooming on the\nbattlefield. It stole the android's heart in an instant,\ncausing emotions he thought lost ages ago to come gushing forth.
weapon.story.wp003503.3: The android fought for the rose, cutting down anything that\nmight cause it harm. He was overjoyed to finally be fighting to\nprotect something, and not to simply take a life.
weapon.story.wp003503.4: When peace finally came, the android realized the red rose was\nthat color because it was splattered with blood. But he still\nwanders the battlefield in an endless search for beauty.
weapon.story.wp003504.1: A cage surrounds me. Walls stop me. My vision is occluded\nby black. I wander the dark, not knowing the way nor my\ndestination. Only my feelings stand out amidst the inky gloom.
weapon.story.wp003504.2: I am made to realize I have stopped wanting. My heart was\nonce spurred on by something long ago, but what?\n I have forgotten; I don't even realize I have done so.
weapon.story.wp003504.3: The paralyzing dark melds into my cavernous heart. \nMy perception and senses warp; my emotions lie languid. \nI am akin to but a husk, but I feel a sense of relief nevertheless.
weapon.story.wp003504.4:
That day, I break through the mud and see a white flower in
bloom. It is far, far too bright, and before I know it, I feel
tears rolling down my cheeks at the sight of it reaching
toward the light.
weapon.story.wp003505.1:
There was once an organization of ninja that served a shogun.
Assassinating enemy lords, silencing allies, executing
vengeance—these were their tasks, and no matter how difficult they
were, they always succeeded.
weapon.story.wp003505.2:
There was one woman in the organization. She chose the path of
the shinobi because she longed to be like her mother, who was a
skilled ninja. She also choose to wield twin blades in order to
better follow in her footsteps.
weapon.story.wp003505.3:
One day, she was ordered to murder her mother, who knew too
much to be left alive. And while a ninja cannot refuse a task,
she wailed as she did the deed, dulling her blows and causing her
mother great pain.
weapon.story.wp003505.4:
Afterward, she reforged her swords and her mother's into one
long blade. As if trying to run from it all, she tried to forget her
mother's dying face and swore on her sword that she would
always kill in a single blow.
weapon.story.wp003506.1:
There was once a kind nobleman. Though he ruled the city,
he never abused his status; he performed his own fieldwork and
chores like any man, and his subjects loved and respected
him greatly.
weapon.story.wp003506.2: The man was always with his people, working hard to make life\nbetter for them. When the waterwheel broke, he repaired it with\nhis own hands. When beasts attacked, he ran to the front lines.
weapon.story.wp003506.3:
But even the finest man cannot stand against nature, and one
season a drought came that withered the crops. Even though the
nobleman had money to purchase food, there was none for
sale anywhere.
weapon.story.wp003506.4: In an act of charity, the man set himself on fire. The hungry\npeople wept before swarming the corpse. Taking a lesson from this,\nthey then began burning and devouring one of their own each day.
weapon.story.wp003507.1:
You know that one hermit who lives outside town? Old guy who
stares out the window when it rains? I hear he was a combat medic
way back in the day. Guy has seen some things,
let me tell you what.
weapon.story.wp003507.2:
This one time, a soldier was brought in covered head to toe in
burns. By all rights the guy should have been dead, and the
army must have thought so as well, because they decided he was
beyond help and didn't treat him.
weapon.story.wp003507.3:
Next morning, they all had to move out, which meant leaving
the burned man behind. The medic—then just a kid—wanted to give
him some water, but the army didn't want to waste any and
ordered him to march instead.
weapon.story.wp003507.4:
I reckon the old guy regrets that to this very day, even
though it was objectively the right decision. That's why
he stares out that window when it rains: he's praying it
falls on the soldier, wherever he is.
weapon.story.wp003508.1: Our immigration fleet had been sailing the stars for months \nwhen we were beset by pirates. My little sister was killed, and \nI now fight with the sword that slew her.
weapon.story.wp003508.2: When I use the sword, I hear a strange voice in my head—a \nvoice that analyzes the current situation and tells me how to \nturn any fight in my favor.
weapon.story.wp003508.3: I obey the voice without question, fighting in a zen state. \nFor some reason, it sounds like my sister. I think she wants \nme to join her.
weapon.story.wp003508.4: Finally, I find the pirate who took her life. The sword orders \nme to kill and I obey—but the moment I do, the voice falls \nsilent, never to speak again.
weapon.story.wp003509.1: People saw the weapon as a useless stick; too heavy for any \nto wield, and too bulky to kill. None even knew why it was \nmade in the first place.
weapon.story.wp003509.2: The weapon was melted down and turned into armor and \nshort swords. Though light, the armor was impenetrable, and \nthough thin, the swords were unbreakable.
weapon.story.wp003509.3: The swords made mountains of corpses; the soldiers in armor\nwere invincible. Each time a life was taken, those doing the \nstealing soared with excitement.
weapon.story.wp003509.4:
But the armor would not come off and the swords could not 
be dropped—and soon the armaments drew together like 
magnets, rolling the soldiers into a hunk of metal bigger than
the original stick.
weapon.story.wp003510.1: The child couldn't get along with his peers. He was bad at \nexpressing things through words, and soon developed a bit \nof a complex with speaking.
weapon.story.wp003510.2: As his poor speech caused him to place distance between \nhimself and others, society treated him as an outcast, causing \nhis loneliness to grow.
weapon.story.wp003510.3: As an adult, he chose a life as hired muscle, knowing none \nwould find fault with silence in such a profession so long as \nhe killed swiftly and well.
weapon.story.wp003510.4: When enemies begged for their lives, he felt human for the \nvery first time. And as he basked in this bliss, a flock of black \nbirds gathered around him.
weapon.story.wp003511.1:
In a desert kingdom filled with goods from far-off
lands and the scent of exotic spices,
a young thief spins a false tale of adventure to the kingdom's
greatest treasure: their princess.
weapon.story.wp003511.2: The thief has finally begun to stir the princess's heart,\nthe passing sun and moon the sole witnesses to their rendezvous.\nAnd when he receives an omen of death, he dismisses it as folly.
weapon.story.wp003511.3:
He spins the tale of what made him a thief.
Of the girl he couldn't save. Then a slave,
he vowed he would never be stolen from again.
It moves the princess greatly, and the two make a secret vow.
weapon.story.wp003511.4:
Having stolen the princess,
the thief runs through the city beneath the moonlight.
They are so close to the sea—so close to freedom.
Yet multiple omens of death pierce the thief's body at last.
weapon.story.wp003512.1:
Can't stick with the boss anymore.
Sneaking into the Thieves' Graveyard?
He's mad! We've been through a lot over the years,
but this is a step too far, even for me.
weapon.story.wp003512.2:
Things fell apart on the way home after escaping the Graveyard.
It was the kid's fault, of course—he treats us like dogs.
Worst part is that he's more
talented than any of us and we know it.
weapon.story.wp003512.3:
Everyone knows who he is: He leads the nation's best thieves
guild and takes everything he wants. The way he acts...
The way he steals...
Every thief in the land wants to be just like him.
weapon.story.wp003512.4:
Finally saw the kid in town. Was relieved to see him alive,
but shocked at how different he was.
What happened to his bejeweled clothes? His sharp gaze?
Did he get a girl? Oh, my brother...
weapon.story.wp003513.1: Once, there was a holy man who loved both children and art. He\nran an orphanage, and spent many a happy day teaching the\nboys there how to paint.
weapon.story.wp003513.2: The holy man often painted the children into his own work,\nexplaining that the beauty of their forms was a kind of art in and\nof itself.
weapon.story.wp003513.3: One day, a boy came to speak with the holy man about changes\nhis body was going through, and the man said they would have a\nfeast in celebration.
weapon.story.wp003513.4: As he prepared their food, he mixed lethal paints into it.\nThis will make it right, he thought, for I am a man who\nloves both art and children.
weapon.story.wp003515.1:
There was once an android soldier who did not fear death.
He wielded a great blade and wandered from battle to battle,
learning how to use his endless life by watching others
being stolen.
weapon.story.wp003515.2: One day, the soldier found a gorgeous red rose blooming on the\nbattlefield. It stole the android's heart in an instant,\ncausing emotions he thought lost ages ago to come gushing forth.
weapon.story.wp003515.3: The android fought for the rose, cutting down anything that\nmight cause it harm. He was overjoyed to finally be fighting to\nprotect something, and not to simply take a life.
weapon.story.wp003515.4: When peace finally came, the android realized the red rose was\nthat color because it was splattered with blood. But he still\nwanders the battlefield in an endless search for beauty.

weapon.story.wp003519.2: I am made to realize I have stopped wanting. My heart was \nonce spurred on by something long ago, but what? I have \nforgotten; I don't even realize I have done so.
weapon.story.wp003519.3:
The paralyzing dark melds into my cavernous heart. 
My perception and senses warp; my emotions lie languid. 
I am akin to but a husk, but I feel a sense of relief
nevertheless.
weapon.story.wp003519.4:
That day, I break through the mud and see a white flower in 
bloom. It is far, far too bright, and before I know it, I feel tears 
rolling down my cheeks at the sight of it reaching toward the 
light.
weapon.story.wp003520.1: A cage surrounds me. Walls stop me. My vision is occluded\nby black. I wander the dark, not knowing the way nor my\ndestination. Only my feelings stand out amidst the inky gloom.
weapon.story.wp003520.2: I am made to realize I have stopped wanting. My heart was\nonce spurred on by something long ago, but what? I have\nforgotten; I don't even realize I have done so.
weapon.story.wp003520.3: The paralyzing dark melds into my cavernous heart. \nMy perception and senses warp; my emotions lie languid. \nI am akin to but a husk, but I feel a sense of relief nevertheless.
weapon.story.wp003520.4: That day, I break through the mud and see a white flower in \nbloom. It is far, far too bright, and before I know it, I feel tears\nrolling down my cheeks at the sight of it reaching toward the light.
weapon.story.wp003521.1: My birthday is on Christmas! Grammy and Grampy are coming over,\nwe're eating yummy food, and I get presents and wear pretty\nclothes! It's sooo much fun!
weapon.story.wp003521.2: My birthday is on Christmas, so I'm going to invite\nfriends over and eat cake. Oh, and I got presents for\neveryone so we can have a gift swap!
weapon.story.wp003521.3: This is my first Christmas with my boyfriend. I've always\nhated having my birthday on this day, but his proposal to\nme made it perfect.
weapon.story.wp003521.4: Fifty years hence, my birthdays aren't so special anymore—but the\nchildren like them, so I do what I can. Still, I've likely only a\nfew more before I join you, so please...wait for me.
weapon.story.wp003522.1: Lady Two is truly kind. She rules the Land of Sands with love for\nher people, and the children love her back—although I am\nundoubtedly the one who loves her the most.
weapon.story.wp003522.2: Lady Two is truly powerful—why, she can defeat monsters with her\nbare hands! I would be no match for her...
weapon.story.wp003522.3: Lady Two is truly faithful—she works so hard in the name of her\nsister's ideals and her people! And she is so straightforward that\nI... I almost went mad with worry.
weapon.story.wp003522.4: Lady Two is truly... She is kind. Too kind. That is why I should not\nhave made her kill the children. That's what I was there for.\nNo matter what happens, Lady Two, I...
weapon.story.wp003523.1:
FILE: e696b0e8a68f
Saw signs of problematic behavior, so previous unit was destroyed.
Made a new clone. Implanted memory of a lonely man.
I wonder what'll happen this time.
weapon.story.wp003523.2:
FILE: e7b58ce9818e
Growth proceeding. Showing signs of skill. Less obedient than ones
with memories of wife/child (son/daughter doesn't matter),
but still within acceptable levels.
weapon.story.wp003523.3:
FILE: e795b0e5a489
He shows no sexual interest in female units,
nor emotional response to males.
What is the problem? I don't think I designed him this way.
weapon.story.wp003523.4: FILE: e5958fe9a18c He caused no offense. No skill problems. His mind is just...elsewhere. Why? What caused this? What are you looking at? Who are you looking at?
weapon.story.wp003524.1: It is the leaves of a plant that make way for the beautiful flowers\nthat follow. This is the woman's bloodline—she is of those who\nexist in secret.
weapon.story.wp003524.2: Her life knows no peace, no normality. Though she acts the part,\nsuch gaps are far too wide to ever be spanned.
weapon.story.wp003524.3: The seaside sun? The smiling people? Such things are too\nbright for her. So she turns away from the light and opens her\nparasol instead.
weapon.story.wp003524.4: A passerby says that her parasol, open as it is toward the sky,\nlooks like a sunflower. How beautiful it is, they say. How utterly\nperfect.
weapon.story.wp003525.1: It is said those who wield this sword will not know fear. Once one\ngrips the handle, heat rises from the depths of their heart and\ntransforms the user into a dauntless lion.
weapon.story.wp003525.2: It is said those who wield this sword will not know defeat. The\nuser does not bend the knee even to a force of tens of thousands,\nand prevails over all who would attempt them harm.
weapon.story.wp003525.3: It is said those who wield this sword will not know aging. Once\nequipped, the sword takes away time as the wielder knows it,\nand throws its wielder into eternal battles.
weapon.story.wp003525.4: Become a lion. Never defeated. Never aging. Rumors beget more\nrumors, and now all manner of tales swirl about this sword. But no\none knows any who have actually wielded the blade.
weapon.story.wp003527.1: There is an old saying passed down through our people:\n"When our bodies crumble to dust, our dignity remains. What\nform this dignity takes depends upon six different emotions."
weapon.story.wp003527.2: Will this saying survive into posterity? Our people sought ties with\nother people—without the threat of war. We formed bonds of\nmutual respect and prayed to live our lives in peace.
weapon.story.wp003527.3:
But they began to lay waste to us, and though some of us
managed to escape, I doubt we will last long. For we have no
weapons and no means to make them, so I expect us to be killed
off shortly.
weapon.story.wp003527.4: But nothing is so senseless as surrendering to death. If there is\nthe chance that I can save the others by sacrificing myself, I will\ngladly do so in accordance with our ancient saying.
weapon.story.wp003528.1: The lord of the house was a devoted man who risked all for\nthe sake of his master. And when the master finally obtained\nprosperity, the lord's family increased in stature with him.
weapon.story.wp003528.2: The lord of the house established a family skilled in the art of\nmurder—a nest of demons—and the techniques and tactics they\nused so proudly were all of his own invention.
weapon.story.wp003528.3: The lord of the house cloaked himself in deepening shadow as\nhis master's glory burned ever brighter. Harsh teachings took root,\nfor one must never take their own personal feelings into account.
weapon.story.wp003528.4: The lord of the house sinned for the sake of a girl who walked a\npath much like his own. Even now, many believe he gave his life\nfor hers.
weapon.story.wp004001.1:
A crying boy beats another who thanks him. Bones shatter.
Blood flies. But it does not stop.
Finally, the boy giving the beating
sees an eyeball on the ground and realizes he is done.
weapon.story.wp004001.2:
The two boys hailed from the same land.
Best friends from a young age,
they grew up experiencing the same things.
But the pair used to be a trio—
until one summer changed everything.
weapon.story.wp004001.3:
As the trio's bodies and minds moved toward adulthood,
things changed,
and the first boy uncontrollably lusted after the second.
The third, unaware of this,
panicked over their changing relationship.
weapon.story.wp004001.4:
When the third boy learned the truth,
he was angry he failed to see
it and so beat the first boy to death.
But the first boy was simply happy to be free
from the pain of losing his friend.
